messages:
alisa_ae: Quick sync — FinLedger (Carol) is looking at an enterprise commit and needs help mapping throughput to reserved GPU sizing + autoscale policy. Current ask: steady 120 req/s, short peaks ~450 req/s for 20–30m, per-request avg ~300 tokens, 95th latency SLO = 600ms. They also want burst credits and a deterministic fallback if capacity is constrained. Carol, added any hard constraints on model choice or region?

carol_customer: We're planning to use an Llama2-70b-like open model variant (quantized) in us-west. In November we expect up to 2x those advertised peaks for a few days. No strict single-AZ requirement, but prefer multi-AZ fallback. SOC2 + KMS for keys is must.

sanjay_se: Thanks. High-level thoughts: reserved pool + burst window looks right. For 300 tokens/request, rough throughput per A100-80GB equiv (quantized) is ~60-90 req/s depending on batching/latency tradeoffs. With 95th 600ms target we need conservative perf numbers. I'd size reservation assuming 120 steady -> estimate 2 GPUs for steady (120 / 60 = 2) and add burst capacity for peaks. For 450 req/s peaks we'd need ~6–8 GPUs to keep latency. Also factor in autoscaler cold-starts and prewarm.

jamie_eng: Adding runtime notes: continuous batching helps a lot but increases tail latency if you overbatch. Recommend a mixed policy: keep N reserved instances hot (no cold-start), allow autoscale to add ephemeral GPUs for burst with prewarm hooks, and use model-fallback (smaller quantized variant) for graceful degradation. Example autoscale policy snippet:```yaml
reserved: 2
max_pool: 10
autoscale:
  scale_up_threshold_rps: 100
  scale_up_step: 2
  scale_down_delay_s: 300
prewarm: true
fallback_model: llama2-13b-quant
```

emily_prodops: For fallback/AZ stuff: enable cross-AZ routing + warm standby in second AZ. Prewarm jobs (e.g., a light KV-cache refill) add cost but avoid cold LRU fills. Also suggest prefix caching for common prompts — that can reduce tokens/gen and load. We can set a burst credit bucket (30min worth of extra GPUs) to allow sustained 450->900 spikes for short windows.

frank_finance: From pricing side: reserved GPU pricing + burst ephemeral hourly rates. Rough monthly calc: If reserve 2 GPUs (committed) + expected 6 ephemeral GPU-hours/day for bursts -> I'll put together a sheet but initial note: committed base will cover steady usage; ephemeral for peaks billed at on-demand effective rate. Prewarm adds additional small hourly cost while running. I'll produce a numbers table after we lock GPU SKU.

sanjay_se: One more perf caveat: token length distribution matters. Our perf numbers use avg 300 tokens; if 10% of requests hit >1k tokens you'll need more headroom. Ask Carol to send a sample RPS token histogram.

carol_customer: I can share anonymized request histogram (we have it). Also: are you able to guarantee no request queueing beyond 200ms during peak? Customer success is sensitive to visible retries.

jamie_eng: We won't guarantee zero queuing, but we can set SLOs and a policy: if queueing predicted >200ms then route to fallback model (smaller) or to a degraded response path (shorter max tokens). That keeps p95 latency bounded. We'll include that in the runbook.

deploy-bot: prewarm-job: scheduled deploy to warm 4 ephemeral nodes at 2026-11-18T08:00Z for FinLedger POC (manual approval pending).

alisa_ae: Next steps: 1) Carol to share token histogram + peak calendar (esp Nov). 2) Sanjay/Jamie to produce two sizing options (conservative + cost-optimized) with SKU assumptions (A100-80GB equiv or H100). 3) Finance (Frank) to create cost worksheet. 4) ProdOps (Emily) to draft autoscale + fallback runbook and burst-credit plan. I'll consolidate and send to FinLedger by EOD Thurs. Sound good? :thumbsup:

carol_customer: Sounds good. I'll drop the histogram here later today. Thanks all.

frank_finance: I'll start a quick model cost calc and post the sheet link once done.

sanjay_se: I'll assume A100-80GB perf for conservative numbers, but will include H100 uplift table.

jamie_eng: I'll draft the autoscaler config & runbook, include exact prewarm TTLs and cache refill steps.

emily_prodops: I'll include cross-AZ warm standby and a note on KMS integration for Private deployments.

alisa_ae: Great — closing loop after those artifacts are in. If anybody wants to pair on the runbook review, ping me. :raised_hands:
